# INPUT
#   DATA/cleaned_quarterly.csv (one row per quarter) with these columns:
#     quarter                   e.g., "1983Q3"
#     quarter_start             first day of the quarter, e.g., 1983-07-01
#     hpi                       FHFA All-Transactions HPI (index points)
#     mortgage_rate_pct         30-year mortgage rate (quarterly average, %)
#     unemployment_rate_pct     Charlottesville unemployment (quarterly avg, %)
#     active_listings           active listing count (quarterly average)
#     hpi_yoy_pct               HPI year-over-year % change
#     mortgage_rate_yoy_pp      mortgage rate YoY change (percentage points)
#     unemployment_rate_yoy_pp  unemployment YoY change (percentage points)
#     active_listings_yoy_pct   listings YoY % change
#
# OUTPUT (all written to the OUTPUT/ folder)
#   PNG figures

#
# HOW TO RUN
#   1. Open the project folder in RStudio (or setwd() to the project
#      root) so that DATA/cleaned_quarterly.csv is found by its relative path.
#   2. Open this .Rmd in RStudio and run the R chunks from top to bottom.
#      Later chunks use objects created in earlier ones.


 


```{r}

# 1. LOAD AND PREPARE THE DATA

# Install any required package that is missing, then load all of them.
# tidyverse supplies dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, readr, purrr, tibble, etc.

 
# Read the cleaned CSV, then:
#  - convert quarter_start to a proper Date,
#  - pull the year and the quarter number (1-4) out of the label
#    "1983Q3" (characters 1-4 are the year, character 6 is the quarter),
#  - sort in time order (lags depend on correct ordering).


library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(scales)
library(purrr)

DATA_PATH <- "DATA/cleaned_quarterly.csv"  # relative to the repository root
data <- read.csv(DATA_PATH)

head(data)
tail(data)

LAST_FULL_QUARTER_START <- as.Date("2026-04-01")   # keeps through 2026Q2
OUT_DIR   <- "OUTPUT"                 # plots and tables are saved here
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
 
save_plot <- function(p, name, w = 10, h = 6) {
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0(name, ".png")), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 200)
  print(p)
}


 
# Create the output folder (does nothing if it already exists).
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)
 
# Use a clean, simple ggplot theme for all figures.
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
 
# Helper: save a plot to OUT_DIR as a PNG and also display it.
#   p    = a ggplot object
#   name = file name without extension
#   w, h = width and height in inches

 

 
```


```{r}


df <- data %>%
  mutate(
    quarter_start = as.Date(quarter_start),
    year = as.integer(substr(quarter, 1, 4)),
    q = as.integer(substr(quarter, 6, 6))      # "1983Q3" -> 3
  ) %>%
  arrange(quarter_start)
  
# Drop partial quarters at the end of the data
if (!is.na(LAST_FULL_QUARTER_START)) {
  df <- df %>% filter(quarter_start <= LAST_FULL_QUARTER_START)
}
 

# Quarter-over-quarter (QoQ) % change in HPI. We use this (not YoY) for the
# seasonality section because YoY comparisons cancel out seasonal patterns.
df <- df %>% mutate(hpi_qoq_pct = (hpi / lag(hpi) - 1) * 100)
 
# Names of the YoY columns. "core" = variables available for the long
# period; "all" adds active listings, which only start in 2016.
yoy_core <- c("hpi_yoy_pct", "mortgage_rate_yoy_pp", "unemployment_rate_yoy_pp")
yoy_all  <- c(yoy_core, "active_listings_yoy_pct")
 
# Define the two analysis windows from our project plan:
#   Long-run = first quarter where HPI, mortgage, and unemployment YoY all exist
#   Recent   = first quarter where listings YoY also exists
# if_all() keeps rows where every listed column is non-missing.
long_start   <- df %>% filter(if_all(all_of(yoy_core), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
                  pull(quarter_start) %>% min()
recent_start <- df %>% filter(if_all(all_of(yoy_all),  ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
                  pull(quarter_start) %>% min()
 
# Store each window's start date and variables in one list for reuse below.
windows <- list(
  `Long-run` = list(from = long_start,   vars = yoy_core),
  `Recent`   = list(from = recent_start, vars = yoy_all)
)
cat("Long-run window starts:", format(long_start), "\n")
cat("Recent window starts:  ", format(recent_start), "\n")
 
# Human-readable labels used for plot titles and axes.
new_names <- c(
  hpi = "House Price Index", mortgage_rate_pct = "Mortgage rate (%)",
  unemployment_rate_pct = "Unemployment rate (%)", active_listings = "Active listings",
  hpi_yoy_pct = "HPI YoY (%)", mortgage_rate_yoy_pp = "Mortgage YoY (pp)",
  unemployment_rate_yoy_pp = "Unemployment YoY (pp)", active_listings_yoy_pct = "Listings YoY (%)"
)
 
```


```{r}

# 2. DATA COVERAGE TABLE
# Purpose: show exactly when each variable starts and ends and how many
# values are missing, since the source series do not line up in time.
coverage <- df %>%
  select(quarter_start, all_of(names(new_names))) %>%
  # Reshape from one column per variable to one row per (quarter, variable).
  pivot_longer(-quarter_start, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    first_quarter = min(quarter_start[!is.na(value)]),   # earliest non-missing quarter
    last_quarter  = max(quarter_start[!is.na(value)]),   # latest non-missing quarter
    n_obs         = sum(!is.na(value)),                  # number of usable quarters
    # Quarters missing in the middle of the variable's span (true gaps).
    n_missing_within_span = sum(is.na(value) &
                                quarter_start >= first_quarter &
                                quarter_start <= last_quarter),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(coverage)

write_csv(coverage, file.path(OUT_DIR, "03_coverage_table.csv"))
```


```{r}
# 3. TIME-SERIES PLOTS (faceted, with recession shading)

# Purpose: see each variable's trend and big events. Each variable gets
# its own panel because their scales differ widely.
shade <- tibble(
  xmin = as.Date(c("2008-01-01", "2020-01-01")),
  xmax = as.Date(c("2009-07-01", "2020-07-01")),
  label = c("Great Recession", "COVID")
)
 
ts_plot <- function(vars, title, name) {
  d <- df %>%
    select(quarter_start, all_of(vars)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-quarter_start, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>%   # draw each series only where it has data
    mutate(variable = factor(new_names[variable], levels = new_names[vars]))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(quarter_start, value)) +
    geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, color = "#2b6cb0") +
    facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +   # separate y-axis per variable
    labs(title = title, subtitle = "Grey bands: 2008-09 recession and 2020 COVID shock",
         x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: FRED")
  save_plot(p, name, h = 9)
}
ts_plot(yoy_all, "Year-over-year changes over time", "04_timeseries_yoy")
 
```


```{r}

# 4. DISTRIBUTIONS AND SUMMARY STATISTICS
# Purpose: see how each YoY variable is spread out (center, spread,
# skew, outliers). YoY is used because raw levels mostly reflect trend.

 
# Long-format data of the four YoY variables for faceted histograms.

yoy_long <- df %>%
  select(quarter_start, all_of(yoy_all)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-quarter_start, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(new_names[variable], levels = new_names[yoy_all]))
 
p_hist <- ggplot(yoy_long, aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#2b6cb0", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free") +   # each variable has its own x and y scale
  labs(title = "Distributions of year-over-year changes", x = NULL, y = "Quarters")
save_plot(p_hist, "06_histograms_yoy")
 
# Summary statistics (n, mean, median, SD, min, max) for each variable
# within each analysis window.

summary_stats <- map_dfr(names(windows), function(w) {
  d <- df %>% filter(quarter_start >= windows[[w]]$from)   # rows in this window
  d %>%
    select(all_of(windows[[w]]$vars)) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
    group_by(variable) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)), mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
              median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
              min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE), max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(window = w, .before = 1)
})
print(summary_stats, n = Inf)
write_csv(summary_stats, file.path(OUT_DIR, "05_summary_stats.csv"))



```





```{r}
#5a. Correlation heatmaps

# ---- 5a. Correlation heatmaps (how do the YoY variables relate?) ----
# For each window, compute the correlation matrix using only the rows
# where all of that window's variables are present.
cor_long <- map_dfr(names(windows), function(w) {
  d <- df %>% filter(quarter_start >= windows[[w]]$from) %>%
         select(all_of(windows[[w]]$vars))
  m <- cor(d, use = "complete.obs")
  # Convert the matrix to long format so ggplot can draw tiles.
  as_tibble(m, rownames = "var1") %>%
    pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "r") %>%
    mutate(window = w)
}) %>%
  mutate(var1 = factor(new_names[var1], levels = new_names[yoy_all]),
         var2 = factor(new_names[var2], levels = new_names[yoy_all]),
         window = factor(window, levels = names(windows)))
 
p_cor <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(var1, var2, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3.5) +   # print the r value in each tile
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#c53030", mid = "white", high = "#2b6cb0",
                       limits = c(-1, 1)) +                  # fixed -1 to +1 scale
  facet_wrap(~window) +
  labs(title = "Correlations among YoY variables", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
save_plot(p_cor, "07_correlation_heatmaps", w = 12, h = 5.5)
 
# ---- 5b. Lagged correlations with HPI growth ------------------------
# For lag k, we compare HPI growth in quarter t with the predictor's
# value in quarter t-k (shifted k quarters earlier). Lag 0 = same quarter.
# This previews "how quickly do prices respond?" without fitting a model.
predictors_all <- setdiff(yoy_all, "hpi_yoy_pct")   # the three predictors
 
lag_cors <- map_dfr(names(windows), function(w) {
  from  <- windows[[w]]$from
  preds <- intersect(predictors_all, windows[[w]]$vars)   # listings only in Recent
  map_dfr(preds, function(p) {
    map_dfr(0:4, function(k) {
      # Shift the predictor by k quarters BEFORE filtering to the window,
      # so early rows in the window still get their earlier values.
      tmp <- tibble(date = df$quarter_start,
                    y = df$hpi_yoy_pct,
                    x = lag(df[[p]], k)) %>%
        filter(date >= from, !is.na(x), !is.na(y))   # use only complete pairs
      tibble(window = w, predictor = p, lag = k, r = cor(tmp$y, tmp$x), n = nrow(tmp))
    })
  })
})
print(lag_cors, n = Inf)
write_csv(lag_cors, file.path(OUT_DIR, "eda_lag_correlations.csv"))
 
# Bar chart of correlation by lag, one panel per predictor and window.
# Blue bars are positive correlations and red bars are negative.
p_lag <- lag_cors %>%
  mutate(predictor = factor(new_names[predictor], levels = new_names[predictors_all]),
         window = factor(window, levels = names(windows))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(lag), r, fill = r > 0)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#2b6cb0", `FALSE` = "#c53030")) +
  facet_grid(window ~ predictor) +
  labs(title = "Correlation with HPI growth by lag",
       subtitle = "Lag k = predictor measured k quarters earlier",
       caption = "Exploratory only: lags are chosen on the same data.",
       x = "Lag (quarters)", y = "Correlation")
save_plot(p_lag, "08_lag_correlations", w = 12, h = 6)
 
```


```{r}


# 6. SEASONALITY: WHICH QUARTER OF THE YEAR LOOKS BEST?
# Purpose: describe within-year patterns. For HPI we use the QoQ change.
# For the other variables we use each quarter's difference from that
# calendar year's average, which removes long-run trends so only the
# within-year pattern remains. Only complete years (all 4 quarters) are used.

# Mortgage rate, unemployment, and listings: deviation from the year's mean.
#   mortgage and unemployment -> difference in percentage points
#   listings                  -> percent above/below the year's average
seas_levels <- df %>%
  select(year, q, quarter_start, mortgage_rate_pct, unemployment_rate_pct, active_listings) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(mortgage_rate_pct, unemployment_rate_pct, active_listings),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(metric, year) %>%
  filter(sum(!is.na(value)) == 4) %>%     # keep only years with all 4 quarters
  mutate(dev = if_else(metric == "active_listings",
                       100 * (value / mean(value) - 1),
                       value - mean(value))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(year, q, metric, value = dev)
 
# HPI: the QoQ % change is already a within-year-comparable quantity.
seas_hpi <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(hpi_qoq_pct)) %>%
  transmute(year, q, metric = "hpi_qoq_pct", value = hpi_qoq_pct)
 
# Combine and attach readable metric labels (factor order sets panel order).
seas <- bind_rows(seas_hpi, seas_levels) %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric,
         levels = c("hpi_qoq_pct", "mortgage_rate_pct", "unemployment_rate_pct", "active_listings"),
         labels = c("HPI QoQ change (%)", "Mortgage rate vs. year avg (pp)",
                    "Unemployment vs. year avg (pp)", "Active listings vs. year avg (%)")))
 
# Boxplots of each metric by quarter of the year (Q1 to Q4).
p_seas <- ggplot(seas, aes(factor(q, labels = paste0("Q", 1:4)), value)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey50") +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#bee3f8", outlier.alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Seasonal pattern by quarter of year", x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = "Listings are only available from 2016, so that panel has far fewer observations.")
save_plot(p_seas, "09_seasonality_boxplots", w = 11, h = 7)
 
# Average, standard error, and sample size for each metric and quarter.
seas_summary <- seas %>%
  group_by(metric, q) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(value), se = sd(value) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")
print(seas_summary, n = Inf)

# ---- Descriptive "buyer-friendliness" scorecard ----------------------
# We rank the four quarters on each metric. "Buyer-friendly" means:
# lower price growth, lower mortgage rate, lower unemployment (a healthier
# job market), and MORE listings (more choice). direction = 1 means
# lower is better; -1 means higher is better. This is descriptive only
# and is not financial advice. Change signs here to alter the definition.
direction <- c("HPI QoQ change (%)" = 1, "Mortgage rate vs. year avg (pp)" = 1,
               "Unemployment vs. year avg (pp)" = 1, "Active listings vs. year avg (%)" = -1)
 
scorecard <- seas_summary %>%
  mutate(signed = mean * direction[as.character(metric)]) %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(signed)) %>%        # 1 = most buyer-friendly quarter for that metric
  ungroup()
 
# Sum of ranks across metrics (lowest total = most buyer-friendly overall).
total_rank <- scorecard %>% group_by(q) %>% summarise(total_rank = sum(rank), .groups = "drop")
print(total_rank)

p_score <- ggplot(scorecard, aes(factor(q, labels = paste0("Q", 1:4)), metric, fill = rank)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = rank)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#9ae6b4", high = "#fbb6b6", breaks = 1:4,
                      name = "Rank\n(1 = best for buyer)") +
  labs(title = "Which quarter looks best for a buyer? (descriptive, not advice)",
       subtitle = "Ranks of average seasonal pattern; flip the rankings for a seller's view",
       x = NULL, y = NULL)
save_plot(p_score, "10_quarter_scorecard", w = 10, h = 4)
 
 

```
